title: The Spark Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 states the outer limit on Spark's self-amendment: "The Spark Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

Three bounds are set at once — the Core Atlas, the Primitive specifications, and the open-ended standard of alignment. The third is the load-bearing one, because it is not exhausted by the first two: an edit can be textually compatible with the Atlas and still be rejected as misaligned. This is the Atlas's spirit-of-the-rule doctrine applied at Agent level, and it is what makes the Facilitator's review a judgment rather than a checklist.

The structural claim is that Agents have real but delegated sovereignty. Spark Governance owns its Artifact and can rewrite it, but only inside a boundary drawn elsewhere and policed by a role it does not control. A conflicting Agent-level rule is invalid rather than an overriding local exception.

The enforcement point is worth noting: the restriction binds through *review*, at the front of the pipeline. There is no described mechanism for invalidating a violating edit that somehow passes review — the design relies on the gate holding.
description: Agent governance is subordinate by construction: alignment with the parent framework and the Sky Primitives is an outer bound on Spark's amendment power, enforced by the Facilitator's review.
